---
title: "Construct Clinic IDs"
subtitle: "Carry reviewed clinic identities across GESIS changes"
execute:
  eval: false
engine: markdown
---

Before DHIS2, there was GESIS.

This page builds the clinic-month identity crosswalk from the
legacy monthly inventory of conditions; the cleaned DHIS2–GESIS mapping; and the reviewed
GESIS corrections. The reviewed rules below remain explicit so their effects
can be checked before the resulting IDs are used downstream.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Make The Legacy Monthly Inventory Available"}

This stage begins by reading in a set of raw data "from Kevin" that is used
to define "unique clinic months".

The cleaned mapping is the `s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df` target from the
preceding page.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare Identity And Input Helpers"}

`targets` tracks the source archive and the rebuilt Parquet inventory as files,
while the mapping dependency uses the preceding page's in-memory data target.
The selectors resolve reviewed inputs from the staged-input inventory rather
than relying on the old script's working directory.

The combined inventory reuses `s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn` from page 18.
It reads with `prudence = "stingy"`, writes the ordered relation, and returns
the tracked output path.

```{r}
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(stringi)
library(duckplyr)

s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE) {
  if (na.rm) x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  values <- unique(x)
  values[which.max(tabulate(match(x, values)))]
}

s2_clinic_ids_first_fn <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0L) NA else dplyr::first(x)
}

```

Require one staged match for each reviewed input, so an ambiguous selection
fails before the corresponding data is read.

```{r}
s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn <- function(paths, pattern) {
  matches <- stringr::str_subset(paths, pattern)
  if (length(matches) != 1L) {
    stop("Expected one staged input matching /", pattern, "/; found ", length(matches), ".")
  }
  matches
}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Select Monthly Archive Members"}

The archived legacy script selects the six identity columns and removes
duplicates within each monthly CSV before combining files. Keeping the health
measurement columns would repeat every identity for each reported measurement.
We perform that reduction in DuckDB and write one Parquet artifact per member.

Only `YYYY_MM.csv` members in `mdg_tall_split/` are selected. This reproduces the
legacy numeric-filename selection for this freeze and excludes `missing_date.csv`,
`diar_pneu_fix.csv`, `AVC.csv`, and macOS metadata. Sorting the members reproduces
the legacy `list.files()` order.

The 120 monthly CSVs in the May 2025 freeze use Windows-1252. A complete byte
scan found `9C`, `A8`, `E0`, `E8`, `E9`, `EB`, and `F4` outside ASCII. For example,
`Ampitafà` contains byte `E0`, and `Sœurs` contains `9C`; the latter distinguishes
Windows-1252 from ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1). A UTF-8 process locale does not change
these file bytes, and Latin-1 is not a valid substitute for this archive.

Use DuckDB's official [encodings extension](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/encodings)
with `encoding = "CP1252"`. `INSTALL` reuses the installed extension after the
first download; a new runtime or DuckDB version needs network access for that
download. `LOAD` runs on duckplyr's own connection in each worker. Decoding
happens in DuckDB before reduction, leaving UTF-8 names in Parquet without
loading the tall CSV into R or skipping invalid rows. The staged archive stays
unchanged.

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_identity_columns_fn <- function() {
  c("cNom", "cAnnee", "cPeriode", "cCodeNiv", "cCodeStru", "fname")
}

s2_clinic_months_list_members_fn <- function(archive_path) {
  members <- utils::unzip(archive_path, list = TRUE)$Name
  members <- members[
    grepl("(^|/)mdg_tall_split/[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}\\.csv$", members) &
      !grepl("(^|/)__MACOSX/", members)
  ]
  stopifnot(length(members) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(basename(members)))
  sort(members, method = "radix")
}

```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Decode And Reduce One Monthly CSV"}

Extract a member into a private temporary directory, decode its identity
fields, and keep the first occurrence of each identity. Only the reduced
Parquet path leaves the branch. The temporary CSV is removed on exit.

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_reduce_csv_fn <- function(csv_path, source_file) {
  # Read text first: read.csv() keeps empty clinic names but treats NA as missing.
  # Cast only the five numeric identity fields, matching the archived integers.
  column_types <- c(
    cNom = "VARCHAR", cAnnee = "VARCHAR", cPeriode = "VARCHAR",
    cCodeNiv = "VARCHAR", cCodeStru = "VARCHAR", cCode = "VARCHAR",
    fname = "VARCHAR", Variable = "VARCHAR", Value = "VARCHAR"
  )
  identity_columns <- s2_clinic_months_identity_columns_fn()
  integer_columns <- setdiff(identity_columns, "cNom")
  duckplyr::db_exec("INSTALL encodings")
  duckplyr::db_exec("LOAD encodings")
  result <- read_csv_duckdb(
    csv_path,
    prudence = "stingy",
    options = list(
      header = TRUE, delim = ",", quote = "\"", escape = "\"",
      types = list(column_types), nullstr = "NA", encoding = "CP1252"
    )
  ) |>
    select(all_of(identity_columns)) |>
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(integer_columns),
        ~ as.integer(if_else(.x == "", NA_character_, .x))
      ),
      .inventory_row = row_number()
    ) |>
    summarise(.inventory_row = min(.inventory_row), .by = all_of(identity_columns)) |>
    mutate(.inventory_file = source_file) |>
    arrange(.inventory_row)

  result
}
```

The branch writer owns extraction and cleanup. It passes the extracted CSV
to the reducer and returns the completed Parquet path.

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_write_member_fn <- function(archive_path, member, output_path) {
  stopifnot(
    length(archive_path) == 1L, file.exists(archive_path),
    length(member) == 1L,
    !grepl("^/|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)", member)
  )

  extraction_dir <- tempfile("clinic-month-")
  dir.create(extraction_dir)
  on.exit(unlink(extraction_dir, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  csv_path <- utils::unzip(archive_path, files = member, exdir = extraction_dir)
  stopifnot(length(csv_path) == 1L, file.exists(csv_path))

  result <- s2_clinic_months_reduce_csv_fn(csv_path, basename(member))

  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}

```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Build The Ordered Monthly Inventory"}

Select the source archive and its monthly members for dynamic branching.

```{r}
#| format: file
s2_clinic_months_raw_zip <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "(^|/)madagascar_clinic_data_cleaning\\.zip$"
)
```

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_members_chr <- s2_clinic_months_list_members_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip
)
```

The execution page declares a dynamic branch per archive member, producing
`s2_clinic_months_deduplicated_parquet`. Each branch extracts into its own temporary
directory and deletes the CSV after the Parquet write finishes. `prudence =
"stingy"` prevents accidental fallback that would materialize raw data in R.
Only artifact paths cross the `targets` boundary.

The combined inventory deliberately retains repeats across files, matching the
legacy procedure. `.inventory_file` and `.inventory_row` record file order and
the first source-row position for each identity. They preserve first-occurrence
tie breaking in the downstream mode calculations; SQL grouping alone does not
guarantee that order.

```{r}
#| format: file
s2_clinic_months_inventory_parquet <- s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn(
  input_paths = s2_clinic_months_deduplicated_parquet,
  output_path = here::here("data", "intermediates", "unique_clinic_months_v1-2.parquet"),
  transform = function(relation) {
    relation |> arrange(.inventory_file, .inventory_row)
  }
)
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Select Reviewed Identity Inputs"}

The correction workbook, reviewed deletions, and verified snips are selected
here for the identity transformations below:

```{r}
#| format: file
s2_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "CSB1 CSB2 PUBLIC PRIVATE\\.xlsx$"
)
```

```{r}
#| format: file
s2_gesis_code_deletions_raw_csv <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "VERIFIER clinic_codes_in_gesis_but_not_in_mapping\\.csv$"
)

s2_gesis_snips_verified_csv <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "GESIS_snips_public_multipleLongGESIS VERIFIED\\.csv$"
)
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Collect The Reduced Identity Inventory"}

Collect only the six identity fields, in original file and row order. This
order determines the first occurrence when the modal identity has a tie.
The tall measurement tables remain in DuckDB and Parquet.

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_inventory_df <- read_parquet_duckdb(
  s2_clinic_months_inventory_parquet, prudence = "stingy"
) |>
  arrange(.inventory_file, .inventory_row) |>
  select(all_of(s2_clinic_months_identity_columns_fn())) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(across(!c(cAnnee, cPeriode, fname), as.character))
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Read And Apply Reviewed Code Corrections"}

Read the correction workbook as character codes, then retain the original
code wherever no replacement was reviewed. Assign the mapping year here:
January–March 2015 and records with `fname == 1` use the old mapping; later
2015 records use the new mapping.

```{r}
s2_gesis_code_corrections_df <- readxl::read_excel(s2_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx) |>
  filter(!is.na(`NEW CODE`), `NEW CODE` != "NEW CODE") |>
  setNames(c("old_code", "correct_code", "uid", "name", "status", "note")) |>
  unique()
```

The corrected inventory carries the selected mapping year into the next join.

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_corrected_df <- s2_clinic_months_inventory_df |>
  left_join(
    s2_gesis_code_corrections_df |> select(cCodeStru = old_code, correct_cCodeStru = correct_code)
  ) |>
  mutate(correct_cCodeStru = coalesce(correct_cCodeStru, cCodeStru)) |>
  mutate(
    map_year = case_when(
      cAnnee == 2015 & cPeriode <= 3 ~ "OLD GESIS 2015",
      cAnnee == 2015 & fname == 1 ~ "OLD GESIS 2015",
      cAnnee == 2015 & cPeriode > 3 ~ "NEW GESIS 2015",
      TRUE ~ as.character(cAnnee)
    )
  )
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Join The Year-Aware Facility Mapping"}

Prepare the identity mapping with its three reviewed exceptions: exclude the
2012–2013 UID match and the invalid old-2015 code, then clear the disputed
2014 UID. Join this mapping on corrected GESIS code and mapping year.

```{r}
s2_gesis_xwalk_identity_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df |>
  filter(!(fs_uid == "gIAGmHMV9MS" & cAnnee %in% c("2013", "2012"))) |>
  filter(!(code_fs == "630242008" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015")) |>
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(code_fs == 110543027 & cAnnee == "2014", "", fs_uid)) |>
  transmute(
    map_year = cAnnee,
    correct_cCodeStru = as.character(code_fs),
    TYPE,
    fs_uid,
    map_name = FS
  )
```

Keep unmatched identities for the UID-fill and name-fallback stages.

```{r}
s2_clinic_months_gesis_mapped_df <- s2_clinic_months_corrected_df |>
  left_join(
    s2_gesis_xwalk_identity_df,
    by = c("correct_cCodeStru", "map_year")
  )
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Fill Unambiguous UIDs And Mapping Attributes"}

Within each corrected-code/name group, fill the UID only when the nonmissing
values identify one candidate. Then fill missing type and mapped name from
their modes within the UID/code/name group. Retain the existing tie behavior.

```{r}
s2_clinic_month_uid_filled_df <- s2_clinic_months_gesis_mapped_df |>
  mutate(
    group_uid = {
      values <- unique(na.omit(fs_uid))
      case_when(
        length(values) == 1L ~ s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(values),
        length(values) == 2L & any(values == "") ~ s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(setdiff(values, ""))
      )
    },
    .by = c(correct_cCodeStru, cNom)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    fs_uid = ifelse(is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == "", group_uid, fs_uid)
  ) |>
  group_by(fs_uid, correct_cCodeStru, cNom) |>
  mutate(across(c(TYPE, map_name), list(uid = ~ {
    mode <- s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(mode) == 1L) mode else NA
  }))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(TYPE = coalesce(TYPE, TYPE_uid), map_name = coalesce(map_name, map_name_uid)) |>
  select(-TYPE_uid, -map_name_uid, -group_uid)
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Assign Provisional IDs And Apply Reviewed Deletions"}

Use the mapped name when present; otherwise normalize the already-decoded
UTF-8 clinic name to ASCII. Prefer a DHIS2 UID and fall back to corrected
code plus cleaned name when the UID is missing.

```{r}
s2_clinic_month_provisional_ids_df <- s2_clinic_month_uid_filled_df |>
  mutate(
    clean_name = ifelse(
      is.na(map_name),
      cNom |>
        stringi::stri_trans_general(id = "Latin-ASCII") |>
        str_trim() |>
        str_squish() |>
        stringr::str_remove("^CSB2|^CSB1|^CSB|CBS") |>
        tolower(),
      map_name
    ),
    clinic_ID = ifelse(
      is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == "",
      paste0(correct_cCodeStru, " - ", clean_name),
      fs_uid
    )
  )
```

Read the reviewed deletion codes and clear the designated IDs without
dropping their rows. The code/year exception for `610351004` is retained.

```{r}
s2_clinic_gesis_deletion_codes_chr <- read_csv(s2_gesis_code_deletions_raw_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(NOTE == "DELETE") |>
  pull(clinic_code) |>
  as.character()
```

```{r}
s2_clinic_ids_corrected_df <- s2_clinic_month_provisional_ids_df |>
  mutate(
    clinic_ID = case_when(
      correct_cCodeStru == "610351004" & cAnnee == 2016 ~ NA_character_,
      correct_cCodeStru %in% s2_clinic_gesis_deletion_codes_chr ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ clinic_ID
    )
  )
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Reconcile Verified GESIS Snips"}

Read the reviewed shortened GESIS codes. Exclude the four ambiguous snips
before joining, then use the modal UID or clinic ID only for verified
groups with more than one identity.

```{r}
s2_clinic_verified_snips_df <- read_delim(s2_gesis_snips_verified_csv, delim=";", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(GESIS_short)) |>
  mutate(GESIS_short = as.character(GESIS_short)) |>
  transmute(
    GESIS_snip = GESIS_short,
    verified_snip = `VERIFIED (1 CORRECT – 0 INCORRECT)`
  )
```

The first reconciliation leaves the commune/name rules for the next step.

```{r}
s2_clinic_ids_snip_reconciled_df <- s2_clinic_ids_corrected_df |>
  mutate(
    GESIS_snip = paste0(str_sub(correct_cCodeStru, 1, 4), str_sub(correct_cCodeStru, 7, 9))
  ) |>
  left_join(
    s2_clinic_verified_snips_df |>
      filter(!GESIS_snip %in% c("1104006", "1104060", "5205039", "5202030")) |>
      filter(verified_snip == "1"),
    by = "GESIS_snip"
  ) |>
  group_by(GESIS_snip) |>
  mutate(
    clinic_ID = case_when(
      n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 & any(fs_uid != "") & verified_snip == "1" ~
        s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(setdiff(fs_uid, ""), na.rm = TRUE)),
      n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 & verified_snip == "1" ~
        s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(clinic_ID, na.rm = TRUE)),
      TRUE ~ clinic_ID
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Reconcile Commune And Clinic Names"}

Combine the commune code with the cleaned clinic name and reconcile the
remaining multiple IDs within that group. Preserve the reviewed 2014
exception for GESIS code `110543027`.

```{r}
s2_clinic_ids_reconciled_df <- s2_clinic_ids_snip_reconciled_df |>
  mutate(
    commune_name = paste0(cCodeNiv, " - ", gsub("^CSB1 |^CSB2 |^CSB ", "", clean_name))
  ) |>
  group_by(commune_name) |>
  mutate(
    clinic_ID = case_when(
      correct_cCodeStru == "110543027" & cAnnee == 2014 ~ clinic_ID,
      n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 & any(fs_uid != "") ~
        s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(setdiff(fs_uid, ""), na.rm = TRUE)),
      n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 ~ s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(clinic_ID, na.rm = TRUE)),
      TRUE ~ clinic_ID
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Write The Clinic ID Crosswalk"}

The final crosswalk keeps the legacy columns and `ID_checked` indicator. Rows
without a clinic ID are retained in the intermediate artifact for review; the
31 expected removals are not silently dropped here.

```{r}
s2_clinic_ids_df <- s2_clinic_ids_reconciled_df |>
  group_by(clinic_ID) |>
  mutate(ID_checked = any(grepl("CSB", TYPE))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    clinic_ID, cAnnee, cPeriode, cCodeNiv, cCodeStru,
    correct_cCodeStru, cNom, fname,
    type_map = TYPE, ID_checked
  )
```

```{r}
#| format: file
s2_clinic_ids_parquet <- {
  path <- here::here("data", "intermediates", "w2010_2019_clinicID.parquet")
  dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(as_duckdb_tibble(s2_clinic_ids_df), path)
  path
}
```

Downstream transformations can consume `s2_clinic_ids_df` directly. The
Parquet copy is tracked with `format = "file"` for disk-based consumers and
inspection. It preserves the crosswalk columns and missing values without
adding a CSV row-index column. The legacy RDS and CSV exports are replaced
by this single Parquet artifact.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Verify Inventory, IDs, And Parquet Persistence"}

Confirm that the completed crosswalk has the expected columns and inspect
missing IDs and type coverage. These queries read completed targets; they do
not create or modify pipeline data. Run them in an authorized data session.

```{r}
tar_read(s2_clinic_ids_df) |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    clinics = n_distinct(clinic_ID, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_ids = sum(is.na(clinic_ID)),
    checked_rows = sum(ID_checked, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

The 31 missing-ID removals noted in the legacy workflow are historical
expectations for review, rather than a newly established assertion.

Verify ordering, cross-file repeats, and Parquet storage with synthetic data:

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript tests/check-clinic-month-parquet-transforms.R
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript tests/check-data-storage-convention.R
```

Run the encoding regression check from the repository root:

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run tests/check-clinic-month-encoding.R
```

The fixture places French characters after the CSV sniffing sample and checks
Windows-1252 decoding, quoted fields, missing values, deduplication, and original
row order against `read.csv(fileEncoding = "CP1252")`. To also compare the complete
January 2010 and January 2015 members against that independent reader:

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run tests/check-clinic-month-encoding.R -- \
  data/inputs/01_gold_mine/gdn_datafreeze_may2025/madagascar_clinic_data_cleaning.zip
```

:::
